name: Bankart Lesion
definition: Detachment of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum, usually after anterior shoulder dislocation and strongly associated with recurrent instability.

investigations.principle: MRI or MR arthrography demonstrates labral injury; CT is used when glenoid bone loss is suspected.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, cartilage, ligament or occult injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Recurrent instability or substantial bone loss may require surgical stabilization.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-Sandhi instability phenotype may be documented after structural diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Detachment of the anteroinferior glenoid labrum, usually after anterior shoulder dislocation and strongly associated with recurrent instability.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, unreduced dislocation, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
